page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs with 2 threads per core, using dedicated CPU allocation to minimize resource contention. System memory is sized at 16.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This instance contains no integrated local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote block storage volumes for persistent data. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because dedicated cores are paired with a balanced memory allocation, the configuration presents a predictable cost-efficiency profile for standard horizontally scaled infrastructure without incurring the operational overhead associated with specialized hardware.

VM.Standard3.Flex.2-16 is suited for mainstream enterprise workloads that do not demand local disk throughput or hardware acceleration. Typical applications include mid-tier web serving, application backends, container orchestration nodes, microservices hosting, and lightweight continuous integration pipelines.
